title: Recurrent In-Stent Restenosis With Localized Coronary PET Uptake: An Etiologic Challenge.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent in-stent restenosis (ISR) may involve localized inflammatory remodeling. Molecular imaging can provide additional information during etiologic assessment.
CASE SUMMARY: We describe 2 patients with ISR in whom multimodality assessment raised the possibility of localized coronary inflammatory remodeling. The first patient had multiple episodes of left anterior descending artery ISR despite repeated drug-coated balloon angioplasty. Fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) showed mild coronary uptake in case 1, who received prednisone after repeat coronary intervention. Fibroblast activation protein inhibitor-PET/CT showed mild coronary uptake in case 2, who had autoimmune serological abnormalities. She received prednisone and hydroxychloroquine, followed by planned coronary recanalization with stent implantation 2 months later. Neither had recurrent angina during 18- and 15-month follow-up, respectively.
CONCLUSION: In ISR, coronary tracer uptake on fluorodeoxyglucose- or fibroblast activation protein inhibitor-PET/CT may prompt consideration of a possible inflammatory remodeling process after major mechanical and conventional clinical causes have been assessed.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Recurrent in-stent restenosis warrants a systematic reassessment of mechanical and biological contributors, including possible inflammatory remodeling, to inform subsequent treatment. In selected patients, PET/CT may complement structural assessment and, when interpreted alongside clinical findings, inform individualized multidisciplinary management.

title: Among-Population Differentiation and East-to-West Decline in Genetic Diversity of Lactarius vividus from Southern China Revealed by Seven Novel SSR Markers.
abstract: Lactarius vividus is a wild edible ectomycorrhizal mushroom widely distributed in southern China, where it forms an obligate symbiotic relationship with Pinus species. However, its genetic diversity and population differentiation remain poorly understood. We collected 95 basidiomata from ten geographic populations spanning seven provinces across an east-west transect of southern China and developed seven SSR primer pairs at the genomic level to investigate its genetic diversity, population differentiation and spatial genetic structure. Genetic diversity showed a clear east-to-west declining trend, being highest in population AQ (Anhui Province) and lowest in KM (Yunnan Province). Observed heterozygosity (Ho) was lower than expected heterozygosity (He) in most population-locus combinations, and many tests showed significant departures from Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium (HWE), indicating a pronounced heterozygote deficit. Analysis of molecular variance (AMOVA) showed substantial population differentiation, with 63% of the total genetic variation occurring among populations. A Mantel test detected a significant positive association between genetic and geographic distances (r = 0.322, p = 0.032), consistent with isolation by distance (IBD). STRUCTURE identified three genetic clusters, while DAPC and UPGMA analyses further revealed geographic differentiation and admixture or genetic overlap among some samples. These findings provide a basis for prioritising geographically distinct populations in the conservation and sustainable management of this wild edible mushroom.
